title: window.ml run export
description: A window.ml session export, schema version 1. GENERATED from export-schema.ts by scripts/gen-export-schema.mjs — do not edit by hand. The TypeScript file is normative; this is its language-neutral twin, for writing a parser or generating models in another language.

$schema.description: URL of the JSON Schema this document was written against, pinned to the COMMIT that produced it — the conventional `$schema` key, which editors (VS Code and friends) pick up to validate and autocomplete a file with no configuration. Pinned to the commit rather than to `main` because `main` drifts away from what this file actually is; a URL that describes a later format is worse than none. BEST EFFORT: it is absent when the build had no git remote or the remote is not GitHub, and when the build was DIRTY the commit's schema is the nearest published thing rather than an exact match — `generator.build.dirty` sitting beside it is how a consumer knows.

schema.description: EXPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION at the time of writing. Check this before parsing.

exportedAt.description: When the export was produced — not when the run happened. Volatile.

name.description: Always "window.ml". Present so an aggregator can tell exports apart by origin.

version.description: The extension version that wrote the file, from the manifest. Coarse — it moves on releases, not on commits. build is what identifies the actual code.

build.description: Which BUILD produced this run. Absent when the exporter had no build stamp to hand.

ExportBuild.description: The commit the extension was built from — the answer to "are these two exports even comparable?". A manifest version cannot answer that: two runs a week apart share it while the code moved underneath. Anything comparing runs (a benchmark sweep, a regression differ) needs the commit, and needs to know whether the tree was dirty, because a dirty build is not reproducible from any commit. Mirrors the extension's own `BUILD_INFO`, minus its `dirtyDiff` unless the exporter opts in — see dirtyDiff.

commit.description: Full commit SHA the extension was built from.

dirty.description: The working tree had uncommitted changes at build time, so `commit` does NOT fully describe what ran. A sweep should treat runs from a dirty build as provisional.

dirtyFiles.description: Paths that were modified, when dirty. Names only — cheap, and usually enough to know what moved.

dirtyDiff.description: The full uncommitted diff, when the exporter asked for it. OPT-IN, and off by default for two reasons: it is frequently larger than the run it describes, and it puts unpublished source into a file that gets shared. Turn it on where the export is a local artifact and reproducing the exact build matters — a benchmark cell, a bug report you are keeping.

buildTime.description: When the bundle was built. Volatile: rebuilding the same commit changes it.

hash.description: The session hash the sidebar shows. Stable within a session, random across them, so a differ comparing two runs of the same task should ignore it.

kind.description: An agent run (a task and its steps) or a chat session (turns).

title.description: The AI-summarised title. Absent when it was never generated.

model.description: The model pinned for the session, when there is one. A per-turn/per-step `model` is the one that actually answered, which can differ (utility profile, server-side resolution).

config.description: The options the session was created with, verbatim: `createChat`'s for a chat, `ml.agent`'s for a run.

anyOf.description: This shape is UNSTABLE: it grows as the extension does and is NOT covered by the schema version. The members here are the ones known when this file was generated — read the ones you recognise and tolerate others.

task.description: The initial task. Agent runs only.

page.description: The page the run STARTED on. Agent runs only, and absent on a run exported from a build that predates the field. Close to a primary key when comparing runs — the same task against a different page is a different experiment — and previously recoverable only by regexing the URL back out of `config.system`, which is prose and only present when `env` was on. A run that navigates ends somewhere else; this is where it began.

taskImages.description: Images attached to the initial task, as data URLs. Agent runs only.

messages.description: The conversation in order: the user's messages and the model's answers. For a chat these are its turns; for an agent run, its `say`s and answers interleaved with the steps by atStep.

steps.description: The agent loop's steps, ordered by seq. Agent runs only.

events.description: The session's TIMELINE — what ran, when, and for how long. Derived; see ExportEvent.

system.description: the resolved system prompt the model actually received

customSystem.description: caller supplied their own `system` (vs the built-in preamble)

tools.description: description/parameters let the sidebar show the FULL tool definitions (a JSON tree), not just names.

vision.description: the `vision` option AS PASSED (true=forced native · false=off · string=forced reader · null=auto)

driverSees.description: RESOLVED: does the driver's own model see the pixels natively this run (native vs delegated look)?

visionModel.description: RESOLVED: the vision reader a delegated sub-call uses (equals the driver when native; null = none)

silent.description: scripting run: kept out of the in-page HUD (the card reads this to stay hidden)

unattended.description: headless run: approval-gated calls are refused (no human to approve)

navigate.description: may this run navigate to other pages (the `navigate` tool + cross-page persistence)? false = off

crossOrigin.description: may this run navigate to OTHER SITES (different origins)? true only when opted in

approvalRouting.description: where privileged gates are resolved: "ui" (default) · "both" (UI + __mlApprovals IPC) · "external" (IPC only)

stream.description: did this run STREAM the model's thinking/reply live (opt-in `stream:true`)? Shown in the agent-options block so you can tell whether a step's "thinking" was live or only landed at the turn's end.

origin.description: Origin of url, split out so grouping by site needs no URL parsing.

ExportOutcome.description: Run-level flags, gathered rather than scattered as optional booleans. DERIVED, and deliberately so: several consumers want these and would otherwise each reconstruct them from different fields and disagree. Every input remains present elsewhere in the document, so a consumer that distrusts our arithmetic can redo it.

hitCap.description: The loop stopped because it reached `maxSteps`, not because it finished.

cancelled.description: Aborted via the HUD or an AbortSignal. The transcript is partial but real.

resumed.description: Resurrected from storage after the service worker was evicted mid-run.

error.description: A FATAL error (the model call failed, or the loop threw). Distinct from a tool returning an error string, which is a normal step result. Null when none.

turnsRun.description: Distinct `step` values, NOT `steps.length` — one loop turn emits several steps (a thought plus one per tool call) sharing a `step`.

ExportTotals.description: Summed counters. Derived for the same reason as ExportOutcome.

steps.description: Step records, i.e. `steps.length`. See turnsRun for the number the loop's cap is measured against.

tokensIn.description: Prompt tokens across the run's own model calls. Excludes delegated sub-calls.

subcallTokens.description: Tokens spent by DELEGATED sub-calls (`look`, `locate`, verify) — billed to the run but not part of the driver's own context.

wallMs.description: ELAPSED wall-clock, first event to last — not time spent working. A multi-turn session includes whatever the human spent between turns, so a chat left open for an hour reports an hour. Dividing tokens by this gives throughput of the session, not of the model. Volatile.

byModel.description: Per-model breakdown, so a sweep can attribute cost when a run used several (a driver plus a utility reader, say).

ExportMessage.description: One conversational message. A chat turn carries both halves (`user` then `assistant`) as two entries so the array reads uniformly for both session kinds.

atStep.description: The cumulative step count when this arrived, so a consumer can interleave messages with steps in the order they happened. Agent runs only.

model.description: Assistant only: the model that actually produced this, after server-side resolution. May differ from model.

extend.description: Assistant only: which profile resolved the model — marks a utility-model reply apart from the default one.

reasoning.description: Assistant only: separate thinking text, when the model emitted any.

sources.description: Assistant only, chat sessions: provenance the server attached (RAG/tool sources).

usage.description: Assistant only: token counts for this turn, when the server reported them.

TokenUsage.description: Token accounting for ONE request, when the server reports it (OpenWebUI returns a `usage` block; Ollama-native returns prompt_eval_count/eval_count). IMPORTANT: `promptTokens` already covers the WHOLE conversation — every turn re-sends the full history — so live context occupancy is `promptTokens + completionTokens` of the LATEST call, never a sum across turns (summing would overcount quadratically). Only cumulative SPEND is a sum.

genMs.description: Wall-clock ms of THIS model call, measured at the source (around the fetch). ALWAYS available; it includes the call's own network/queue latency (TTFT) — the honest "time spent waiting on the model".

evalMs.description: Ollama-native `eval_duration` (generation-only, ns → ms) when the native route reports it. PREFERRED over `genMs` for a tok/s rate (it excludes network/queue); absent for cloud / OpenWebUI-OpenAI.

loadMs.description: Ollama-native `load_duration` (ns → ms): how long THIS call spent loading the model before generating. Small and constant when the model was already resident; seconds-to-a-minute when it was not — which is the difference between "the model was slow" and "the model wasn't there yet", and the only place that answer exists. Absent for cloud / OpenWebUI-OpenAI, which don't report it.

promptEvalMs.description: Ollama-native `prompt_eval_duration` (ns → ms): reading the prompt, before a token comes back. Real model work, and it scales with the conversation — a system prompt re-sent every turn is paid for every turn. It is the difference between a model that is slow to answer and a BOX that is slow to reach: without it, `genMs - evalMs` lumps prompt eval together with queue and network, and a gap between two models cannot be attributed to either. Absent for cloud / OpenWebUI-OpenAI.

genPhases.description: WHAT the model was doing across this call, when we could observe it — see GenPhase. STREAMED CALLS ONLY: a non-streaming response is one object with one `eval_duration`, which says how long the generation took but not when it stopped thinking and started answering. Splitting that by text length would be inventing a timestamp, so it stays absent and the surfaces draw one undifferentiated block.

GenPhase.description: One stretch of a generation, by what the model was emitting: its thinking channel, its reply, or the fragments of a tool call. A MARK, not a span: `atMs` is where the phase STARTED, as an offset from the call's own start, and it runs until the next mark (or the end of the call). Offsets rather than absolute stamps so the marks stay meaningful without carrying a clock alongside them, and so they line up with `genMs` — which is measured from the same origin — instead of drifting against it. A SEQUENCE, deliberately, not three buckets. Models interleave: reasoning resumes after a tool call's fragments, and a run that thinks-calls-thinks is a real shape. Bucketing would collapse the re-entry and draw one long block that never happened.

kind.description: `think` the reasoning channel · `answer` the reply content · `call` tool-call fragments.

atMs.description: Offset in ms from the START of the model call.

ExportStep.description: One agent step: either a thought, or a tool call with its arguments and result. Transient view state is NOT exported — `pending`, `awaitingApproval`, `liveStream`, `ended`/`endedStep` describe a live UI, not the run. A pending step never appears in an export; only its completed form does.

step.description: The loop turn this belongs to. Several steps share one.

localStep.description: Index within the current turn of a multi-turn session (`run()` then `continue()`), where `step` keeps counting across turns.

seq.description: Groups the records a single model turn emitted: a thought and the tool call it decided on share one `seq`. It is therefore NOT unique — 9 records over 5 turns carry 5 distinct values — so it identifies a turn's event group, not a record. ORDER: the `steps` array is already in the order things happened. Sort by `seq` only with a stable sort, or ties reorder; array order is authoritative.

durationMs.description: How long the tool took, from `toolMs`. Frequently ABSENT — the loop records it per tool call, and a thought-only record has none. Volatile.

thought.description: The model's narration for this step, when it produced any.

tool.description: The tool called. Absent on a thought-only step.

arguments.description: The arguments the model emitted, verbatim — not normalised, not re-ordered.

argIssues.description: Schema complaints about those arguments (required/type/enum/unknown-prop), as the sidebar's red strip shows them. Absent when the args were clean.

result.description: The fuller captured output — what the UI shows, which can exceed what the model received (see modelResult).

modelResult.description: What the model ACTUALLY received, when it differs from result — the result is clipped to a context budget while the UI keeps more. Omitted when the two are identical. Required by the project's raw-view rule: an export must always carry the model-facing text, never only the prettier one.

streamOutput.description: Output the tool streamed as it worked, when it streamed.

streamMarks.description: `[offsetInStreamOutput, epochMs]` per line, stamped by whatever produced the output. Lets a consumer reconstruct per-line timing. Volatile.

token.description: The `@tool:<id>` token minted for this output, when one was, so a citation in an answer can be resolved back to the step that produced it. Volatile.

approval.description: How a privileged call was approved: auto-approved by the read-only interpreter or sandbox, consented by origin, approved by the user, denied, and so on. Absent when the tool needed no approval.

grants.description: Grants this step created / reused, for privileged fetches.

elements.description: A COUNT of matched DOM elements. Never the nodes: they cannot cross the bus.

feedback.description: What was fed back into the model's context off the back of this step (a crop after a `locate`, say), and why.

usage.description: Token counts for the model call that produced this step. In practice this sits on the THOUGHT record of a turn, not on the tool call it led to — the tokens were spent deciding, and the tool call is the consequence. Do not expect it per tool. `session.totals.tokensIn` sums these, so it counts the re-sent conversation once per turn. That is what a run COST; it is not the count of distinct tokens.

subUsage.description: Tokens spent by delegated sub-calls made DURING this step.

PersistGrant.description: A persistable egress consent a tool call would establish — the unit button #3 remembers for the session. Extracted STATICALLY, background-side (grant-extract.ts), so it holds only literal targets the human saw. `kind` keys the UI's per-kind rendering + the background's per-kind persistence (today: `ml.fetch` URLs).

urls.description: the distinct static URLs this grant would remember

ReusedGrant.description: A prior grant a tool call REUSED (so it ran without a fresh prompt) — the transparency counterpart of PersistGrant. `kind` keys the per-kind label/icon; `detail` is the human-readable thing reused (the URL, the sheet name/id). Extensible: a new grant kind adds a `kind` + a detail here + one render branch.

LocateSubstep.description: One stage of a `locate` run: a vision sub-call (grid cell-pick, Set-of-Marks pick, grounding box) or a non-model DOM snap. A sub-call carries its `prompt` (In), the model's raw `output` (Out), the exact `rawImage` sent, and a human `image` overlay (the raw⇄visualise toggle). A DOM snap carries just `image` + `label` (no prompt).

label.description: header after the [N] badge, e.g. "Cell pick · grid 5×3 · model chose cell 12"

note.description: grey-italic explanation shown ABOVE this substep (e.g. why a hand-off happened)

prompt.description: In: the prompt sent to the model (collapsible)

image.description: the visualise (human overlay) view — shown by default

rawImage.description: the exact image sent to the model; its presence enables the raw⇄visualise toggle

TablePreview.description: One loaded DataFrame for the `python-in` render: its variable name, its source, and either a rows preview (`columns`+`rows`) or `html: true` (loaded via `pd.read_html`, no clean preview).

FetchAttempt.description: One rung of the Markdown ladder, as it actually ran. Recorded for every attempt — including the ones that were skipped — because the failure modes here are INVISIBLE in the body alone: a stub twin is a valid 200 Markdown document that is simply the wrong page, and a site-authored twin is content written specifically to be read by agents (GitBook appends an "Agent Instructions" section), so "which URL did these bytes come from" is provenance for an injection surface, not decoration.

strategy.description: `accept` = the same URL with `Accept: text/markdown`; `declared` = the `<link rel="alternate">` the page named; `sibling` = the derived `.md`/`index.md`; `convert` = our own HTML→Markdown.

ToolFeedback.description: What a tool fed back INTO the model's context, for the debug render + export to surface (the model received it via the normal channels — an inline image, or appended result text). `locate`'s snap-inject sets it: a marked crop (vision driver) or a delegated description (text-only driver), plus the `reason` it was sent (a point is automatic; a selector/@box only when `verify:true`).

image.description: the marked crop (data URL) — shown in the render even for a text-only driver (what got described)

prompt.description: the exact prompt the reader was asked over the crop (via:"text") — shown in the debug render + export

label.description: Human-readable, as the panel labels it — the model id for a generation, the tool name for a step.

endedAt.description: When it ended. Absent on an instant (a point on the timeline, not a span) and on an event that had not finished — open tells those two apart. Volatile.

durationMs.description: `endedAt - at`, which is the number a timeline is usually read for. Absent on an instant, and on an open event, which has elapsedMs instead. Volatile.

open.description: This had NOT FINISHED when the document was written — a model still generating, a tool still running, a person still at an approval gate. Present only in a snapshot of a live session (see `ExportProvenance.includeInFlight`); a document of finished work never contains one. It is a separate flag rather than a missing `endedAt` because that spelling already means an INSTANT, and the two are opposites: one is a moment with no duration, the other a duration with no end yet.

elapsedMs.description: How long an open event had been going, measured to the document's `exportedAt`. Deliberately NOT `durationMs`: that field means a measured length, and a consumer summing the two together would be adding a fact to a reading that is still moving. Volatile.

model.description: The model that did the work, where one did. A sub-call names the READER, not the driver.

id.description: This event's own id, and the event that SPAWNED it — a sub-call's parent is its step, a step's parent is the run. Following `parent` gives the lineage the panel lights up on hover. Opaque, and unique within this document only. They EMBED the session hash, which is volatile — pass strings through canonicalizeText before diffing, which handles it.

seq.description: The step this came from, matching seq — how a timeline event gets back to the record that produced it. Absent on events that belong to the session as a whole.

tool.description: The tool that ran, on a `tool` event. Same value as label, named so a consumer switching on `kind` need not know that.

phases.description: A `tool` event's parts, in the order they happened and contiguous from at. Durations rather than absolute ends, since that is what they are read as. Volatile.

cost.description: What it cost, on the kinds that spend tokens.

kind.description: This shape is UNSTABLE: it grows as the extension does and is NOT covered by the schema version. The members here are the ones known when this file was generated — read the ones you recognise and tolerate others.

tokPerSec.description: Output tokens per second. Absent when nothing timed the call. Volatile.

genBasis.description: Which clock tokPerSec came from: Ollama's own generation timing, our wall clock, or a mix across several calls. A rate that silently mixed the two would imply a precision it does not have. Absent alongside the rate.

evalMs.description: Ollama's generation-only time and our wall clock for the SAME call, when both are known. Volatile.

promptEvalMs.description: Reading the prompt, before a token came back. Real model work, and it scales with the conversation — a system prompt re-sent every turn is paid for every turn. It is here because the remainder is otherwise uninterpretable: `wallMs - evalMs` is prompt eval PLUS queue PLUS network, and those are not the same kind of thing. Prompt eval belongs to the model and should count against it; queue and network are facts about the box and the moment. As one number a difference between two models cannot be attributed to either. Volatile.
